utterances.text: Definitely. This is a very crucial point in the Holbrooke-Milosevic Agreement, that it was only negotiated with Milosevic and did not include the Kosovar Albanians. So they did not feel obliged by this agreement that -- that that was a big problem in the whole set-up and there was not -- there was not enough done on the part of the international community to engage the military side of the Kosovar Albanians. That was the problem at the time. So therefore, they had a chance to move back into where the Yugoslav forces had left.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention to a "Joint Proposal of the Agreement on the Political Framework of Self-Governance in Kosovo and Metohija" dated on the 20th of November, 1998. You'll see that at tab 24, which is Exhibit 1D91. Now, you knew about the existence of this agreement at the time; correct? Are you familiar of it? Let me refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew of it. We have seen it at the time, but since then I have not revisited it. This is the first time now.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Then in fairness to you let's look at the first page and perhaps the three first paragraphs may help refresh your memory with dates and events. The first paragraph reads: "The political solution to the problems in Kosovo and Metohija was considered in Pristina on 18 November and in Belgrade on 19 November with a delegation of" certain parties. Further down, I won't read them all -- and further in that same paragraph: "As well as with the representatives of the socialist party of Serbia and the president of the Serbian Radical Party and the Yugoslav United Left Party. President Milutinovic also held consultations on the same issue on 20 November with the presidents of the Serbian renewal movement, New Democracy, and Alliance of the Vojvodina Hungarians. At these talks and consultations, full support was given to the agreement between President Milosevic and Ambassador Richard Holbrooke, particularly to the political framework for the resolution of problems in Kosmet expressed in 11 points of the government of Serbia. Also many concrete comments and suggestions were made on the ways to achieve and institutionalise a political solution to the problems in Kosovo and Metohija." Now, this may help refresh your memory that this was the culmination, this agreement was the culmination of all these events, including your shuttle diplomacy, at this point on the 20th of November. Would that be a fair --

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I mean, this proposal is a joint proposal between those parties which are listed above, which I -- which we referred to earlier on that they unfortunately did not represent the majority of Kosovar Albanians in Kosovo and the Government of Serbia. It has nothing to do with the international paper, Hill, and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting that this document includes those other groups. I'm not suggesting that it was a final agreement or even one that was suggested.

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: What I am suggesting to you is that this, as we've followed the evolution of this process since the creation of the Markovic delegation and your involvement with Ambassador Hill and your drafts, this agreement is the fruits of that process, is it not?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was done totally without Hill and myself, so I am not aware that anything of what we did was really actively involved in here or taken up. Might be; I do not know. I have not studied it, but it was indeed a joint proposal by those specific parties of Kosovo and the Government of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: In the preambulary language I just read to you, there was reference to the 11-point Milosevic-Holbrooke Agreement. And I would ask you to turn to tab 25 which is Exhibit 1D204. And that's a letter sent by the permanent mission of Yugoslavia to the UN addressed to the President of the Security Council. And attached to that is the 11-point document.

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: That came about as a result of the meetings held between Ambassador Holbrooke and President Milosevic in early October and I think you've probably seen this document with the 11 points before.

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And this is the document that led to the arrival of the OSCE, as we've heard; correct?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And we see that in the fourth paragraph of this document on page 2. The sixth paragraph says: "In addition a political framework has been worked out. An agreement has been reached on the principles of a political solution and on a timetable framework for its realisation which is an important achievement." So, Ambassador, what we have here is --

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I could not find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you again point to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: It's the second page of this exhibit, 1D204.

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: At the top of the second page it says: "Annex." Do you see that? Tab 25 for you.

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Tab 25.

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: 25, yes. "Annex, Serbian government endorsed accord reached by President Milosevic."

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: If you go down to the sixth paragraph, beginning: "In addition."

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: "A political framework has been worked out. An agreement has been reached on the principles of a political solution and on a timetable framework for its realisation, which is an important achievement." Now, this Holbrooke-Milosevic document, doesn't it represent in addition to the Milosevic-Yeltsin agreement in June a second foray into having the international community involved?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was seen as an important next step. It got both the OSCE involved and NATO. There were two agreements, one with OSCE and the other one with NATO for surveillance -- NATO surveillance mission over Kosovo. And that -- and this, so to speak, the civilian part was the so-called agreement with -- included the 11 points which President Milutinovic put forward and which, by the way, later on then became part of the so-called non-negotiable principles, which I drafted and also included the relevant points from the 11 points of President Milutinovic. So these -- this is a very important next step that had been taken on the part of the Serbian government.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And if you turn to the next page. I'm thinking -- I'm looking at paragraphs 5, 6, and 7. You don't have to look at them in detail but I would ask you just to peruse them quickly. We're talking there about setting up a future in Kosovo and Metohija based on equality, self-governance, and legal frameworks, and the invitation to the OSCE to supervise elections to ensure their openness and fairness.

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Correct?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: The last point I want to look at in this document with you is the timetable. It said: "By Wednesday, October 14th, a comprehensive timetable will be agreed upon building on the following elements" --

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, now, I'm at a loss again -- oh, timetable, it's down here, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I should direct you better I'm sorry. October 19th there's the agreement on the OSCE. On the next page by 2nd of October: "The completion of an agreement containing core elements for a political settlement in Kosovo and Metohija using as a basis the paper proposed by the Contact Group, 2 October 1998." We've just looked at, Ambassador, the proposal for settlement dated 20 October. Now, it may be 18 days late but we can see that the commitment of the timetable was fairly close, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Are you aware that on the 25th of November, 1998, in Pristina, the delegation -- Professor Markovic's delegation and representatives of minority groups again went back to Pristina, and there Mr. Milutinovic chaired a meeting where there was a signing of a declaration in support of this joint proposal or agreement. 25th of November, does that sound familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, unfortunately I cannot recall this but I can imagine that this took place, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: That's at tab 26. Sixteen, the declaration may help refresh your memory. Tab 26 is Exhibit 1D18 from the Weller book, e-court 372. You see the text of the --

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: -- declaration, who was present.

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And then the signatories. You see Dr. Markovic.

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You see that people of the minority groups living in Kosovo and Dr. Kutlesic, who as we know is the Special Envoy of President Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Right?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And my position is that this, of course, did not end the process. It was an important building-block in the process because, if we turn to tab 27, which is 1D18, 373 to 379, it's the Hill proposal of the 2nd of December, 1998. So clearly the process was not finalised. You and Professor -- Ambassador Hill were still working, but I'm sure that you took into account what -- the joint proposal we looked at on the 20th of November, I'm sure you probably had a look at that when you were revising the Hill proposal. Would that be --

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a matter of routine, clearly we contacted both sides before we issued a new draft proposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Now, I've been suggesting to you that the state delegation and the minority groups who supported the state were being constructive. I would also put it to you that people like Mr. Demaqi were being destructive. Would you agree with that in this period during this process?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is true but again you need to keep in mind whom they represented and whom Mr. Demaqi and who Mr. Rugova represented. The problem was always that the majority did not join these efforts and was never convinced, neither by the Serb government nor by the international community, to get engaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Did you consider Ambassador Hill to be unfamiliar with the Albanian question?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Did you consider him deficient and in need of being replaced?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Let's look at tab 28. Exhibit 1D, the Weller book, e-court 379. On the right-hand column you see: "Kosova press release. Demaqi rejects Hill's plan 8 December, 1998. Now here's what Mr. Demaqi says about Ambassador Hill: "Mr. Chris Hill is either unfamiliar with the Albanian question or else is taking sides with the Serbs, accommodating their demands," Demaqi says. "The UCK representative urged the State Department, if it is possible, to review the work of Mr. Holbrooke and Mr. Hill, especially the latter, and find people who do not have the prejudices of Dayton, who do not have some deficiencies which we see as the cases of such oscillations which have astonished the Albanian and international public. Demaqi said he would like the State Department to review Hill's record and possibly find a man who would be free of the past and committed to serious efforts in pursuit of a real solution, a solution that would be lasting against the backdrop of the Albanian/Serb contest." Now, would you agree with that description of Ambassador Hill?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all, but it attests to the fact that Ambassador Hill tried to do an objective, professional job, not getting a clause from either side just to see to it that a just and equitable compromise is being worked out. Clearly more extreme positions like the one from Demaqi would not be happy about this, and that's a sign of the quality of the draft for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Let's look at the last sentence of this declaration: "Adem Demaqi said it was his historic mission to unite the Albanians so that we would be united in force and politics and create our state." Now, you know that his vision was more than an independent Kosovo; he wanted to unite Albanians across Macedonia, Kosovo, and Albania; correct?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were ideas. There were and are ideas out there that range from a Greater Serbia to a Greater Albania. This is something which is indigenous to this region but has no whatsoever relevance for the reality on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And the -- for the UCK to achieve this they would have to affect three sovereign states, wouldn't they: Macedonia, FRY, and Albania.

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, and that was clearly something that the international community ruled out. At the time, 1998/1999, we were working for a solution within the internationally recognised borders of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Petritsch, if you go below the centre of this press release to the end of the quotation from Demaqi, you'll see that it's claimed: "He is very much in agreement with the position the chief Kosovo negotiator Fehmi Agani took with regard to the latest Hill draft plan. I think the time has come for us Albanians to offer our own proposal that we ourselves offer our assistance to the solution of this problem." A very odd quotation from him at this stage in the matter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not say so. Dr. Agani, he's, as I said before, the main negotiator on the Kosovar Albanian part, a trusted aid of Mr. Rugova, basically expressed what he was -- what his opinion was. And indeed, if I remember correctly, the December draft, the last one that they are referring to there, we were trying to accomplish as much possible from -- from the Serb side. We reached out as far as we thought it is possible yet at the same time clearly we were of -- very much aware that this will meet the protest of the Albanian side. But we tried it out nevertheless; this is the nature of any such shuttle diplomacy and mediation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The impression -- the reason I ask the question was, the impression might be taken from this statement that they had not until then offered any assistance to the solution of the problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't get that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't -- the reason I asked you the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- is that one might read this as an indication that up until that point in time the Albanians had not offered any assistance to the solution of the problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. What -- what Agani's indicating here is that they would not simply feed in their ideas into -- into our proposals, but basically would come up with their very own initiative so to speak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because there they realised they thought that now they are being crossed and therefore that -- that, in my opinion, is reflected in this text, which I see the first time here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Ambassador, let's move to Rambouillet. And you've told us that this process came about as a result of the meeting of the Contact Group held in London on the 29th of January, 1999; correct?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And we've heard evidence in this case about key dates and personalities, but to give you and those of us present here some context at tab 29 as Exhibit 1D16, which is a calendar of the month of February. It's there to assist you if -- if you need it. You're covering lots of material here today.

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: But you told us that the conference began on Saturday the 6th of February?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And ended on Tuesday the 23rd; correct?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And we've also been told that initially it could have been a one-week process. It was extended a second week, until the 20th, Saturday, the 20th, and yet again until Tuesday, the 23rd. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And the meeting was extended on the 20th following a meeting of the Contact Group which was held at Rambouillet?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And the six Contact Group countries were the US, the UK, France, Germany, Russian Federation, Germany, and Italy?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And the co-chairs were Mr. Vedrine and Mr. Cook from the -- France and the UK respectively. We know that you were a member of the troika with Ambassadors Hill and Mayorski; correct?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And at the time Germany held the Presidency of the EU. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Exhibit P2792 is your interview with the Prosecutor of this Tribunal and at page 2 you said this: "In February the Serbian negotiating team at Rambouillet had a mandate to compromise and to come to an agreement on the political aspects of the proposal, i.e., the question and level of autonomy for Kosovo." At page 3 you state more precisely: "At Rambouillet the Serb delegation had a mandate to negotiate the political agreement but they were clearly not mandated to negotiate about the implementation of such an agreement." Now, my question is whether you are familiar with the conclusions of the Serbian Assembly of the 4th of February, 1999, which established this delegation and created its mandate. Are you familiar with this -- these conclusions of the 4th of February?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall them.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You don't recall hearing about those?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there is -- I knew about it but now, I mean, it's too long away that --

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: No, I won't ask you to recite it chapter and verse, but you knew that -- that the Serbian -- the National Assembly had debated the issue --

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: -- and discussed it and come to its conclusions on whether or not to attend --

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: -- and who to send and what their mandate would be. Is that a fair summary that you ...

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Tab 31 is 1D93, Ambassador, and it's the conclusions of the assembly -- National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia of the 4th of February, 1999, and --

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's --

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: -- it's at tab 31 for you and 1D93 for e-court. And it's a rather lengthy document that I will not take you through it in great detail. But if you turn to paragraph 10. Do you have paragraph 10 in front of you? That makes reference to this joint proposal of the 20th of November, 1998, and the declaration in Pristina of the 25th of November?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: 1998. Paragraph 11 says: "Concerning the demand that the parties accept the level and nature of international presence deemed appropriate by the international community, the National Assembly wishes to note the level and nature of this international presence in Kosmet has been ultimately defined in the agreement between the president of the FRY, Slobodan Milosevic, and Ambassador Richard Holbrooke in the agreement between the federal government and the OSCE on the establishment of the OSCE verification mission in Kosmet in accordance with it." Now, this reflects the position as you knew it on the 4th of February; correct?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Paragraph 14 the National Assembly points out that: "Any demand for substantial or high degree of self-governance for Kosmet not only in further negotiations cannot lead to independence for Kosovo and Metohija or a status of a third federal unit, but that this autonomy can simply cannot imply the severance of legal, political, economic ties within the Republic of Serbia." You were aware of that position, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: If we turn to the section headed by V, if you can find that, V, paragraph 2 (ii), the National Assembly of Serbia once again re-affirms the principles on the basis of which the crisis of Kosovo and Metohija can be resolved successfully, durably, and in the interests of all." Then there's a number of bullet points. We see the reference to political means and dialogue, full respect for territorial integrity and sovereignty, full equality, harmonisation with constitutions and legislation, no independence, and the last point at the bottom of the page: "We do not accept the presence of foreign soldiers in our territory under any pretext of implementing the achieved agreement." Now, you were aware of this position, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of this specific point here that you just made.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Could you explain to us, how could it be that you were one of the negotiators, a representative of Contact Group at Rambouillet, and you were not aware of the conclusions passed by the -- adopted by the government two days before the conference took -- how is that possible -- the Assembly, sorry. The Assembly.

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- what is expressed in this paper here in the conclusions of the National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia does not really bring anything new. So we were, of course, aware that there is resistance against any military presence there. We had for weeks on end negotiated that the unarmed international presence would be -- to this would be added an armed component. And we were at one point quite close to this, but we never succeeded for KVM to achieve this. And the background again to this is that while the international community was there unarmed, the armed conflict escalated and it was clear - clear to everybody - that one would in the end need a military component in order to pacify Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I think you've answered my specific question already, but my question was quite specific. You knew about the position adopted by the National Assembly in regard to no foreign troops. You knew about that?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew about the Serb position on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Thank you. This -- these conclusions also appoint a delegation and at tab 32, Exhibit P967, we have the members of that delegation named. Do you see that, Ambassador?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And you -- those are the names you are familiar with --

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that --

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: People you spent time with in the lovely castle in the south of Paris?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Professor Markovic was the head of the delegation, and I note the persons listed at 6, 7, 8, 9, and 11 and 12 are from the Muslim, Turkish, Goran, Albanian, Roma, and Egyptian communities; correct?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Now, exhibit -- one moment, please. Tab 30 for you, Exhibit P979.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Tab 30. P979. That's the statement of the Contact Group from 29 --

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: -- January 1990 in London which summoned the parties to Rambouillet; correct?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I'm looking at paragraph 3(D). Do you see that paragraph, 3(D)?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Three lines up from the bottom it says: "The Contact Group recognises the legitimate rights of all other communities within Kosovo." By that they mean the non-Albanian majority; correct?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And we've seen that the Serbian delegation has representatives from not only the Serb and Albanian groups but the minorities?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and was very welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes. And of course the Kosovar Albanian delegation at Rambouillet was only made up of Kosovar Albanians, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WOLFGANG PETRITSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, are we breaking at 1.45?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We will have to because there's another case here in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Well, this may be a convenient place for me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It may -- you've got a fair distance to go still, eh?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not suggesting we stay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would the change from yellow tabs to blue tabs have any significance? Did you run out of yellow ones?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I think the container got empty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. In an ideal world we would carry on for another session today but we can't because we don't have the space. It's as simple as that. We have to sit in shifts in this court --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have to go back and do my work in Geneva but of course I'm at your disposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we need tomorrow morning, again at 9.00, and hopefully we will complete it. Mr. O'Sullivan, I understand, has a far longer cross-examination than any other counsel and there may only be two other counsel with a number of questions for you and then re-examination by the Prosecution. So can I invite you with regret to leave again with the usher and we'll see you tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And, Mr. O'Sullivan, your efforts to rectify the record, so far as your exhibits are concerned, failed again.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And it should be, I think, P559.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: That's correct, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
